name: City of Jewels
epithet_and_role: lost city of jewels; capital and home of the player's previous incarnation; hub of all the Empire's administration — without it the empire would fracture
features: made by the great Law Giver; the Sumerian ending razes its foundations
map_status: off-map in v1 (D-002/D-005): known only through people; rumour; caravans and the past-life flashback device (round-2-invented.md); its ruin is visited only in the hidden ending (endings §3.4)
real_site_correspondence: Akkad — its real location is itself lost to history; the notes' own §11.7 candidate and the only city whose real-world site is unrecoverable like the fictional one
source_ref: D-018; wb §4.1;§5; notes L15;L42; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of the Dead
epithet_and_role: home of the biggest ancestor cult; underworld queen cult and dead cult in all of the Empire
features: streets filled with skulls; dog and owl engravings ward houses; biggest assortment of ritual scrolls for speaking with underworld spirits; greatest temple built within the earth with a great statue of the queen of the underworld
map_status: off-map in v1; reachable through people; caravans and rumours (README pattern); a future city-by-city expansion candidate given its dramatic weight (gugalanna)
real_site_correspondence: Kutha — the real Mesopotamian underworld/Nergal cult city; the closest real analogue to a city built around death and the netherworld
source_ref: D-018; wb §5; notes L44; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of the Sky
epithet_and_role: cult center of the Sky Father An and the Lady of the Skies on top of a sacred hill; one of the oldest cities; first city on which the northerners lowered kingship
map_status: off-map in v1; reachable through people; caravans and rumours
real_site_correspondence: Uruk — An/Anu's principal real-world cult city and one of the oldest Sumerian cities; matching 'one of the oldest cities'
source_ref: D-018; wb §3;§5; notes L46;L58; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of Kings
epithet_and_role: hub of the god of kings Enlil; center from which the legacy of kings is mummified and guarded
features: the Garden of the Gods (biggest temple of all the gods — every aspect of creation present); massive underground catacombs where the greatest kings join the ancestors in the Kingdom of the Dead
map_status: off-map in v1; reachable through people; caravans and rumours
real_site_correspondence: Nippur — Enlil's real cult center and traditional seat of Mesopotamian kingship's legitimacy
source_ref: D-018; wb §3;§5; notes L48;L59; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of the Sun
epithet_and_role: headquarters of the guild of paladins
map_status: off-map in v1; reachable through people; caravans and rumours
real_site_correspondence: Larsa — a real cult city of Utu (alongside Sippar) and one of the notes' own 'five first cities'
source_ref: D-018; wb §5; notes L50; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of the Moon
epithet_and_role: capital of the enigmatic Prophet; home of the rebellious alliance of southern city states; one of the oldest and the richest (direct sea trade routes)
features: temple of sun and moon; the Great Lighthouse; hub of trade and scholarship
map_status: v1 map (D-005): the player's arrival city and the fully simulated slice; ~20 km² region per D-002
real_site_correspondence: Ur — Nanna/Sin the moon-god's real cult city; the Prophet is 'a seer from the city of Ur' (notes L19); confirming the pairing directly
source_ref: D-005; wb §5; notes L19;L52; D-018 (the site pairing is the notes' own, elevated from OPEN to confirmed); jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of the Abyss
epithet_and_role: the oldest city in the lands; also called the city of Mystics
features: worship of primordial water since the dawn of creation; shifted from the two waters to the Water Lord and the Swamp Queen
map_status: off-map in v1; reachable through people; caravans and rumours
real_site_correspondence: Eridu — the real oldest Sumerian city and Enki's cult center; matching 'the oldest city in the lands' exactly
source_ref: D-018; wb §3;§5; notes L54;L58-59; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: City of the Warrior Spirit
epithet_and_role: once the city of the former sun god of the Taurissian people
features: now ruled by a mighty warchief of the eastern barbarian alliance
map_status: off-map in v1 (it lies in the eastern barbarian lands; outside the region map even at growth); known only through raiders; refugees and rumour
real_site_correspondence: none — it is a Taurissian (the Empire's own people) city; not a Sumerian one; it keeps only its canon name
source_ref: D-018; wb §4.3;§5; notes L56; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)

name: e-ab-kur-irkalla-ki = Gravestone
epithet_and_role: home of the cult of the dead
features: home of the earth mother of the underworld. Ruling (D-018): this IS the City of the Dead — one city, its native cultic name (see deities.csv:underworld_queen)
source_ref: D-018; wb §5; notes L103; jurisdiction column INVENTED (D-018, W2-A city-life §3.1 map moved to canon in the wave-2 review)
